title: Smallest Range Covering Elements from K Lists
summary: Given k sorted integer lists, determine the smallest range that includes at least one element from each list.
statement: Given k sorted integer lists, determine the smallest range that includes at least one element from each list. The range [a, b] is considered smaller than [c, d] if b - a < d - c or a < c when b - a equals d - c.
constraints: 1 <= len(nums) <= 3,500; every inner list is nonempty and sorted.
The range must contain at least one value from every list; break equal-width ties by the smaller left endpoint.
reference_solution:
def smallest_covering_range(nums):
    import heapq
    heap = []
    current_max = -float('inf')
    for list_index, values in enumerate(nums):
        heapq.heappush(heap, (values[0], list_index, 0))
        current_max = max(current_max, values[0])
    best = [heap[0][0], current_max]
    while True:
        current_min, list_index, value_index = heapq.heappop(heap)
        if (current_max - current_min, current_min) < (best[1] - best[0], best[0]):
            best = [current_min, current_max]
        if value_index + 1 == len(nums[list_index]):
            return best
        following = nums[list_index][value_index + 1]
        current_max = max(current_max, following)
        heapq.heappush(heap, (following, list_index, value_index + 1))

target_time_complexity: O(total values * log number of lists)
hints: A candidate range is determined by the current minimum and maximum across one value per list.
Keep one cursor per sorted list in a min-heap and remember the current maximum.
Pop the minimum, update the answer, then advance only that value’s list.
Only advancing the list holding the minimum can shrink the range; stopping at an exhausted list is unavoidable.
